newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says on track with DASA on Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says on track with DASA on Eurofighter.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that Bonn was making progess in talks with Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) on temporary financing for the Eurofighter warplane.
"I think that we are on a good track with DASA to guarantee financing," Waigel told a news conference.

Bonn is trying to plug a two billion mark funding shortfall in the 23 billion marks cost of buying 180 Eurofighters. It has had to delay ordering the aircraft because of financing problems caused by Germany's efforts to meet the criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU).
DASA, the German partner in the four-country Eurofighter project, has threatened to stop work if there is no official funding before the parliamentary summer recess.
Trade union leaders at the Paris airshow said on Monday the delay was putting around 50,000 jobs at risk in Europe and threatened all of Europe's aviation and space industry.
Waigel has already reached an informal agreement with Defence Minister Volker Ruehe that half the shortfall will be covered by the defence budget.

On Monday, DASA chief executive Manfred Bischoff told a German daily that his company, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, could help with the financing by making early repayments of state financing for the Airbus civilian jet.
